claims.text: WTaMoNbV is proposed as an aluminum-free refractory high-entropy alloy base system.
The aluminum-free WTaMoNbV base alloy oxidizes non-protectively at extreme temperatures.
Adding approximately 2–5 at.% Al will improve the high-temperature oxygen resistance of the refractory HEA.
The added Al will promote formation of a continuous and adherent Al2O3 surface scale.
The proposed protective scale will be thin, dense, and continuous.
Preferential oxidation of added Al is thermodynamically favorable.
The resulting Al2O3 layer will be slow-growing and adherent.
The Al2O3 layer will impede oxygen diffusion into the alloy.
Restricting oxygen diffusion will suppress oxidation of the other alloy constituents and reduce mass gain and degradation.
Relative to the untreated alloy, the Al-doped alloy will have significantly lower mass gain and a more uniform protective Al2O3 scale.
An untreated refractory HEA forms non-protective mixed oxides and undergoes rapid degradation at 850–900 °C in air.
The beneficial effect is expected during exposure to laboratory air at approximately 850–900 °C for about 100 hours.
Excessive Al addition might alter the alloy's mechanical properties or phase stability.
The proposed test compares an undoped base alloy with an otherwise identical alloy containing approximately 3 at.% Al in laboratory air at 850 °C for 100 hours.
Mass gain, oxide-scale thickness and continuity, and oxide phase composition will be measured using gravimetry, cross-sectional SEM, and XRD.

The hypothesis is declared falsified if the Al-doped alloy shows no statistically significant mass-gain reduction and does not form a continuous, predominantly Al2O3 scale relative to the undoped control.
